cleanup: Release any owned Control wait normally; join all already dispatched requests before any data cleanup.
Delete only the three-or-fewer tracked fixture roots storage and verify empty KV; Control is cleaned last and must have zero waiters/timers.
An unsettled trace or cleanup requires bounded external owned-process reap and store removal; it never earns runtime credit.
External supervisor verifies final process/store teardown; fixture cleanup alone does not prove it.
contract.distinct: This is an already-live object and ordinary per-request block rather than constructor readiness or storage.transaction. The second same-class root directly distinguishes root-local admission from class-global blocking. No native gate contention, reentry or failure scenario is recreated.
fixed_assertions: c.eq((await c.send(target,'seed')).value,'seed','ordinary target is initialized before the request gate');
c.eq(held.targetId,target.id.toString(),'request hold belongs to the already live target');
c.eq((await c.send(peer,'seed')).value,'seed','a second root of the same class remains serviceable during the live request block');
c.eq([before.phase,before.entries.length,writer.settled,reader.settled],['held',0,false,false],'reader does not enter while the successful critical section awaits control');
c.eq(results.map(x=>[x.value,x.explicitRelease]),[['committed',true],['committed',true]],'reader observes the terminal write after ordinary gate release');
c.eq(after.entries.map(x=>[x.request,x.afterRelease,x.ready,x.targetId]),[['reader',true,true,target.id.toString()]],'actual reader admission is recorded after release with terminal local state');
c.eq(after.fallbackUsed,false,'no fallback timer supplied request completion');
contract.oracle: The same-class peer completes before release, the held target admits no reader, and the reader enters after explicit release with committed terminal state. No intermediate value can satisfy the fixed oracle.
